Bank of America places holds on deposited checks to give the bank time to validate the check and confirm the funds [2]. This helps protect you from potential fees if the check turns out to be unpaid.

Holds typically last 2–7 business days, depending on the reason [1]. You'll be notified about the hold through your deposit receipt, ATM screen, email, or mail—depending on how you deposited the check [5].

Important to know: even after funds become available to you, a check may still be returned unpaid later [2]. And Bank of America service reps can't release funds while they're on hold, since the validation process is still underway [4].

results.answer:
When you deposit a check via mobile, funds are generally available the next business day [2]. Here's what matters:

- If you deposit before the cutoff time on a business day, it processes that night and is available the next business day [2]
- Cutoff times depend on your time zone: 9:00 p.m. ET (Eastern/Central) or 8:00 p.m. PT (Mountain/Pacific) [1]
- Deposits made after cutoff or on weekends/holidays process the next business day and are available the following business day [2]

A hold may delay access beyond the next day if the bank needs extra time to validate the check [4, 7].
